components.title: Azure Bastion (Standard SKU)
components.description: Managed, browser- and native-client jump host providing SSH/RDP access to the private SPARC VM over TLS without any public IP or SSH key on the VM itself. Deployed via Terraform (Azure/VM/modules/bastion/), opt-in via enable_bastion. Uses a dedicated AzureBastionSubnet and a single Standard zonal public IP; sessions are audited to Log Analytics. Serial Console access is available as a complementary path (subscription/portal-enabled) via the VM's boot diagnostics. <!-- UPDATE: Insert the Bastion host resource ID, public IP, and Log Analytics workspace ID for your deployment. -->

control-implementations.description: NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 control implementations for Azure Bastion

implemented-requirements.description: Remote Access: Azure Bastion is the managed remote-access path to the SPARC VM. The VM has no public IP and no inbound SSH from the internet; operators connect through the Bastion over TLS (443) from the Azure portal or the native client (az network bastion ssh/tunnel). This centralizes and controls all remote administrative access. Reference: DISA SRG-APP, CIS Azure. <!-- UPDATE: confirm no public IP on the VM NIC. -->
implemented-requirements.remarks: Terraform: azurerm_bastion_host.main (sku Standard, tunneling_enabled) + azurerm_public_ip.bastion in Azure/VM/modules/bastion/. VM remains on the private subnet with no public IP (vm/networking modules).

implemented-requirements.description: Remote Access | Monitoring and Control: All Bastion sessions are recorded to Log Analytics via a diagnostic setting emitting the BastionAuditLogs category, providing automated monitoring of remote-access sessions (who connected, when, and to which target). Reference: DISA SRG-APP-000516.
implemented-requirements.remarks: Terraform: azurerm_monitor_diagnostic_setting.bastion with enabled_log category BastionAuditLogs, targeting the Log Analytics workspace from the monitoring module.

implemented-requirements.description: Event Logging: Bastion session and management events are captured as auditable events (BastionAuditLogs) and retained in the Log Analytics workspace alongside the VM, NSG-flow, and platform logs, supporting after-the-fact investigation of remote-access activity. Reference: DISA SRG-APP-000089.

Least Functionality: The Bastion host disables file copy (file_copy_enabled=false) and shareable links (shareable_link_enabled=false), restricting the session feature set to interactive SSH/RDP and clipboard. Native-client tunneling is enabled for administrative access without broadening the VM's network exposure. Reference: CIS Azure, DISA SRG-APP-000141.
implemented-requirements.remarks: Terraform: azurerm_bastion_host.main with file_copy_enabled=false, shareable_link_enabled=false, copy_paste_enabled=true, tunneling_enabled=true.

implemented-requirements.description: Boundary Protection: Bastion runs in a dedicated AzureBastionSubnet (minimum /26) and is the sole administrative entry point to the private VM subnet. The single Standard, zone-redundant public IP is the only public endpoint in the access path; the VM subnet has no direct internet inbound. Reference: DISA SRG-NET-000364, CIS Azure.
implemented-requirements.remarks: Terraform: azurerm_subnet.bastion (name AzureBastionSubnet) in the networking module + azurerm_public_ip.bastion (Standard, zones 1/2/3).
